name: CNOT as a row operation
summary: A CNOT on the outputs of two spiders corresponds to adding the neighbourhood of one spider to that of the other.
description:
Consider spiders that are each connected to one output, and to some other spiders by Hadamard edges, described by a biadjacency matrix $M$ over $\mathbb F_2$. Adding the row of the first spider to the row of the second (toggling every Hadamard edge of the second spider to a neighbour of the first) and then applying a CNOT on their outputs, with the target on the first, leaves the diagram unchanged.

This is the key step of the circuit-extraction algorithm for graph-like diagrams: Gaussian elimination of the biadjacency matrix of the frontier is turned into a CNOT circuit. Duncan, Kissinger, Perdrix and van de Wetering also show that the rule preserves focused gflow.
parameter_notes: Shown for two spiders with two neighbours each, one of them shared. Holds for any neighbourhoods; the neighbours may have any further legs and edges.

source.location: Section 7 (Circuit extraction for general circuits), Proposition (CNOT and row operations)
